name: Integer overflow in allocation size (unchecked multiplication into malloc/realloc)
attack_scenario: An attacker supplies a large count so count*size wraps past SIZE_MAX to a tiny value; malloc returns a small buffer, then the code writes count elements into it, giving a heap overflow that overwrites adjacent allocator metadata or objects and leads to RCE (classic CVE-2002-0639 / OpenSSH-style integer-overflow-to-heap-overflow).
negative_test_hint: request an allocation of count = "4611686018427387904" elements of size 4 and assert the code detects the wrapping product instead of allocating an undersized buffer it then overflows

exemplar.explanation: CERT C MEM07-C ('Ensure that the arguments to calloc(), when multiplied, do not wrap') and INT30-C, plus ANSSI's 'Regles de programmation pour le developpement securise de logiciels en langage C', warn that computing an allocation size as the product of two runtime values can wrap a size_t, allocating far fewer bytes than the later loop writes. Patterns anchor to malloc/alloca/realloc whose size arg is IDENT*IDENT closed by ')' (sizeof is excluded because it is followed by '(' not ')', and digit literals are not [A-Za-z_]), so calloc(n, m), malloc(n * sizeof(int)) and single-operand sizes never match. Medium confidence: the product may be range-checked upstream, so it is a review vector rather than a certain bug.
